summary: Lower derived-class instance fields after super() returns, avoiding C# field initializers whose execution order is earlier than JavaScript.

target.notes: Emit uninitialized C# storage and explicit assignments immediately after base construction returns and before the remainder of the JavaScript derived constructor. Do not use C# instance field initializers for these JS fields.

semantics.js_order: base constructor first, then derived fields, then constructor remainder
semantics.csharp_hazard: C# derived field initializers run before base constructor

caveats: This is a critical JavaScript/C# ordering difference; using `int x = 1;` or similar on the C# derived field is incorrect when the base constructor can observe the derived object.

tests.name: base cannot see derived initialized value
tests.input: class B { constructor(){ console.log(this.x); } } class D extends B { x=1; } new D();
tests.expected_behavior: base constructor observes undefined for x; x becomes 1 only after super returns

tests.name: edge: derived initializer before post-super body
tests.input: class B {} class D extends B { x=1; constructor(){ super(); console.log(this.x); } } new D();
